lines: Mind the bottles. Some are medicine, some are mistakes I have not named yet.
Give the brewing stand room. Remedies works better without elbows in it.
Step carefully near the brewing stand. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
There you are. I was just near the brewing stand, trying to keep the day sensible.
Morning. Or afternoon. The work makes the hours blur if I let it.
Good to see you walking in calmly. That usually means nothing is on fire yet.
If you need me, speak up. If you need gossip, speak quieter.
You caught me before the next little disaster. That is rare timing.
Hello. Try not to bring the whole village into this unless it is important.
I have a moment. Not a long one, but a real one.
Come in gently. The bottles are calm and I would like them to stay that way.
Hello. If you need quiet, there is room for it.
I was listening to the brewing stand complain. You may be easier.
Step carefully. Healing tools should not become new injuries.
Peace to you, or at least a fair attempt at it.
You look like you have brought a question with weight on it.
I have a moment between remedies. Speak plainly.
Welcome. Leave the door as you found it if you can.
The room is warm and the water is clean. That is a decent start.
Hello. I can listen while the stand finishes its work.
If this is urgent, say so first.
Come closer if you mean no harm.
I was sorting herbs. They are less complicated than people, but only slightly.
You have my attention. Use it kindly.
Let us speak before the day grows sharper.
